The Sea

The sea does not argue;
it folds, unfolds, folds again,
a patient letter written
and washed blank.

It borrows every footstep
and gives nothing back
but salt, and the long
white punctuation of foam.

By night it holds the moon
the way a hand holds a coal—
careful, and knowing
it will burn through.

The Sea

The sea does not promise;
it only moves, and moves again,
a long exhale under the moon.

Salt on the wind,
a gull's thin cry
scattered like foam.

It takes what it is given —
old storms, small boats, names
we speak once and forget.

And still it holds the horizon
like a hand cupping light,
and asks nothing back.

0/2:
The Sea

The sea does not speak,
but it keeps a language
in the drag and hush of waves—
a word for every ship
that ever forgot the shore.

It pulls the moon down nightly,
like a lantern lowered
to find the lost,
and in the morning leaves
salt on the windows
of the world.

Come, stand at the edge
where the land gives out.
Everything here
is either leaving
or coming back.
